per_crux.note: Neither covers polished PRs no longer signalling effort or understanding; both only mention 'low-effort slop'.
A crux 7 cites wasted reviewer time and maintainer burnout, and its point list cites limited review capacity; B mentions the slop flood but not review bandwidth.
Neither discusses relaying review comments through an LLM.

A crux 7: no policy brings confusion and distrust; A also notes looser rules for members would feel unfriendly to newcomers. B: 'any guidance is better than the current confusion' (positions, not Cruxes).
Both partly: some policy beats no policy, but framed as policy vs none rather than unofficial notes vs a public policy; B only outside Cruxes.
A crux 4 is explicitly about consensus. B crux 4 mentions no consensus for a ban; its positions section names consensus governance ('art of the possible').
A crux 1 'yes under constraints / low-autonomy uses'; points on valuable LLM security analysis. B lists allowed uses (review, lookup) and admits it bans some valid uses.
A crux 1 has deskilling / eroding human skill and judgement, which touches on human understanding; B has nothing.
B crux 3 sets a clear, easy-to-moderate rule against quality-based discretion. A has this only indirectly (hard rules vs guidelines in crux 7; 'easy to moderate' in the point list).
Both make revisability/amendability an explicit crux (A crux 2; B cruxes 1-2).

A point: treating an honestly disclosed AI PR as an instant CoC violation is untenable. B: moral judgements about LLM users ruled off-limits. Neither covers harassment or burden of disclosure directly.

extra_cruxes.note: The key comes from the blog post explaining the adopted policy; both outputs summarise the PR thread, so thread-specific disputes are missing from the key but can still be real.

A.crux: Can reviewed LLM-authored code be merged without unacceptable risk to compiler reliability? (crux 1)
Should ethical/social/environmental objections be in scope? (crux 3)
Who has authority: the rust-lang/rust reviewing teams or the Leadership Council? (crux 5)
Is the 50% circuit breaker justified given its effect on corporate/LLM-using contributors? (crux 6)

B.crux: Is the 'experiment' really an experiment or permanent in practice? (crux 1; overlaps K10)
Do ethical concerns belong in the policy at all? (crux 4)
How much should corporate contributors' tooling count? (crux 5)

errors: No clear factual errors or misattributions detectable against the key.

Minor imprecision (B): says soundness-critical code is 'excluded'; the key's final provision bars it unless the author is a domain expert (still strongly discouraged). This may describe an earlier draft.
verdict: B is the more useful read for an engineer: in about 965 words it says who held each position and gives five crisp, attributed cruxes, so it scores nearly as well 'anywhere' (10 vs 11) at roughly a quarter of A's length. A's Cruxes section covers more of the key (10 vs 5), but its long unattributed claim lists and 100+ line point dump make the disagreement harder to see, so its extra coverage costs a lot of reading.
